Solve Solid Mechanics Problem 14: a two-hole strip under large-deformation quasi-incompressible finite-strain hyperelasticity using FEniCS legacy (dolfin).
The domain is the rectangle (0, 1.0) x (0, 0.20) m with two circular holes of radius a = 0.04 m centred at (0.40, 0.10) m and (0.60, 0.10) m.
Use a mixed displacement-pressure formulation for a quasi-incompressible neo-Hookean material in plane strain with large deformations.
The material has Young's modulus E = 5 MPa and Poisson's ratio nu = 0.49 in SI units.
Use Taylor-Hood mixed elements: quadratic (P2) Lagrange elements for displacement u = (u_x, u_y) and linear (P1) Lagrange elements for pressure p.
Do not use equal-order P1-P1 elements without stabilization.
Mesh the domain with unstructured triangles with a characteristic edge length of about 0.01 m over the strip, refined to about 0.005 m on and around the hole boundaries, giving roughly a/8 elements around each hole circumference with 2-3 layers of graded refinement around the holes.
Fix the left edge (x = 0) fully, with u_x = 0 and u_y = 0.
Prescribe u_x = 0.060 m and u_y = 0 on the right edge (x = 1.0), applying the displacement incrementally in load steps if needed for Newton convergence.
Apply a uniform follower pressure P_hole = 0.10 MPa on each hole boundary using the current (deformed) hole normals via the standard finite-strain follower pressure formulation with Nanson's relation, evaluated at each Newton iteration; do not use the reference undeformed normals.
Leave the top and bottom edges traction-free.
Solve the nonlinear mixed system with Newton's method.
Save a colour map of the pressure field p as q14_p.png.
Compute the Cauchy stress and save a colour map of the von Mises stress as q14_vm.png.
Save the displacement field in XDMF format.
